note: SYNTHETIC ENGINEERING CONTROLS written for the benchmark, not the learner's notes. They check that the configuration step can say 'fits' at all, and still refuses an obvious mismatch. They are never counted as real-note results.

excerpts.text: Binary search works on a sorted array. It compares the target with the middle element; if the target is larger it keeps the right half, otherwise the left half, and repeats until it finds the target or the range is empty.
excerpts.objective: Binary search halves the search range of a sorted array at each comparison

excerpts.text: Bubble sort repeatedly compares adjacent elements and swaps them when they are out of order. After each pass the largest remaining value has moved to the end of the array.
excerpts.objective: Bubble sort moves the largest remaining value to the end on each pass by swapping adjacent elements

excerpts.text: Linear search checks each element of the array in turn, starting at index 0, and stops at the first element equal to the target. If no element matches it reports -1.
excerpts.objective: Linear search returns the index of the first match, or -1

excerpts.text: Arrays are indexed from zero, so for an array of n elements a[0] is the first element and a[n-1] is the last. Reading a[n] is outside the array.
excerpts.objective: Zero-based array indexing: a[0] is the first element and a[n-1] the last

excerpts.text: A hash table stores each key in a bucket chosen by a hash function. Two keys that hash to the same bucket collide, and chaining keeps both in a linked list in that bucket.
excerpts.objective: Hash collisions are resolved by chaining keys in a bucket's linked list

expected.reason: hash tables and chaining are not in the algorithm module
